44: fn strip_prefix(uri: &Uri, prefix: &str) -> Option<Uri> {
45:     let path_and_query = uri.path_and_query()?;
46: 
47:     // Check whether the prefix matches the path and if so how long the matching prefix is.
48:     //
49:     // For example:
50:     //
51:     // prefix = /api
52:     // path   = /api/users
53:     //          ^^^^ this much is matched and the length is 4. Thus if we chop off the first 4
54:     //          characters we get the remainder
55:     //
56:     // prefix = /api/:version
57:     // path   = /api/v0/users
58:     //          ^^^^^^^ this much is matched and the length is 7.
59:     let mut matching_prefix_length = Some(0);
60:     for item in zip_longest(segments(path_and_query.path()), segments(prefix)) {
61:         // count the `/`
62:         *matching_prefix_length.as_mut().unwrap() += 1;
63: 
64:         match item {
65:             Item::Both(path_segment, prefix_segment) => {
66:                 if prefix_segment.starts_with(':') || path_segment == prefix_segment {
67:                     // the prefix segment is either a param, which matches anything, or
68:                     // it actually matches the path segment
69:                     *matching_prefix_length.as_mut().unwrap() += path_segment.len();
70:                 } else if prefix_segment.is_empty() {
71:                     // the prefix ended in a `/` so we got a match.
72:                     //
73:                     // For example:
74:                     //
75:                     // prefix = /foo/
76:                     // path   = /foo/bar
77:                     //
78:                     // The prefix matches and the new path should be `/bar`
79:                     break;
80:                 } else {
81:                     // the prefix segment didn't match so there is no match
82:                     matching_prefix_length = None;
83:                     break;
84:                 }
85:             }
86:             // the path had more segments than the prefix but we got a match.
87:             //
88:             // For example:
89:             //
90:             // prefix = /foo
91:             // path   = /foo/bar
92:             Item::First(_) => {
93:                 break;
94:             }
95:             // the prefix had more segments than the path so there is no match
96:             Item::Second(_) => {
97:                 matching_prefix_length = None;
98:                 break;
99:             }
100:         }
101:     }
102: 
103:     // if the prefix matches it will always do so up until a `/`, it cannot match only
104:     // part of a segment. Therefore this will always be at a char boundary and `split_at` wont
105:     // panic
106:     let after_prefix = uri.path().split_at(matching_prefix_length?).1;
107: 
108:     let new_path_and_query = match (after_prefix.starts_with('/'), path_and_query.query()) {
109:         (true, None) => after_prefix.parse().unwrap(),
110:         (true, Some(query)) => format!("{}?{}", after_prefix, query).parse().unwrap(),
111:         (false, None) => format!("/{}", after_prefix).parse().unwrap(),
112:         (false, Some(query)) => format!("/{}?{}", after_prefix, query).parse().unwrap(),
113:     };
114: 
115:     let mut parts = uri.clone().into_parts();
116:     parts.path_and_query = Some(new_path_and_query);
117: 
118:     Some(Uri::from_parts(parts).unwrap())
119: }

121: fn segments(s: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
122:     assert!(
123:         s.starts_with('/'),
124:         "path didn't start with '/'. axum should have caught this higher up."
125:     );
126: 
127:     s.split('/')
128:         // skip one because paths always start with `/` so `/a/b` would become ["", "a", "b"]
129:         // otherwise
130:         .skip(1)
131: }
132: 
133: fn zip_longest<I, I2>(a: I, b: I2) -> impl Iterator<Item = Item<I::Item>>
134: where
135:     I: Iterator,
136:     I2: Iterator<Item = I::Item>,
137: {
138:     let a = a.map(Some).chain(std::iter::repeat_with(|| None));
139:     let b = b.map(Some).chain(std::iter::repeat_with(|| None));
140:     a.zip(b)
141:         // use `map_while` when its stable in our MSRV (1.57)
142:         .take_while(|(a, b)| a.is_some() || b.is_some())
143:         .filter_map(|(a, b)| match (a, b) {
144:             (Some(a), Some(b)) => Some(Item::Both(a, b)),
145:             (Some(a), None) => Some(Item::First(a)),
146:             (None, Some(b)) => Some(Item::Second(b)),
147:             (None, None) => unreachable!("take_while removes these"),
148:         })
149: }
150: 
151: #[derive(Debug)]
152: enum Item<T> {
153:     Both(T, T),
154:     First(T),
155:     Second(T),
156: }

367:     #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
368:     struct UriAndPrefix {
369:         uri: Uri,
370:         prefix: String,
371:     }
372: 
373:     impl Arbitrary for UriAndPrefix {
374:         fn arbitrary(g: &mut quickcheck::Gen) -> Self {
375:             let mut uri = String::new();
376:             let mut prefix = String::new();
377: 
378:             let size = u8_between(1, 20, g);
379: 
380:             for _ in 0..size {
381:                 let segment = ascii_alphanumeric(g);
382: 
383:                 uri.push('/');
384:                 uri.push_str(&segment);
385: 
386:                 prefix.push('/');
387: 
388:                 let make_matching_segment = bool::arbitrary(g);
389:                 let make_capture = bool::arbitrary(g);
390: 
391:                 match (make_matching_segment, make_capture) {
392:                     (_, true) => {
393:                         prefix.push_str(":a");
394:                     }
395:                     (true, false) => {
396:                         prefix.push_str(&segment);
397:                     }
398:                     (false, false) => {
399:                         prefix.push_str(&ascii_alphanumeric(g));
400:                     }
401:                 }
402:             }
403: 
404:             if bool::arbitrary(g) {
405:                 uri.push('/');
406:             }
407: 
408:             if bool::arbitrary(g) {
409:                 prefix.push('/');
410:             }
411: 
412:             Self {
413:                 uri: uri.parse().unwrap(),
414:                 prefix,
415:             }
416:         }
417:     }

420:         #[derive(Clone)]
421:         struct AsciiAlphanumeric(String);
422: 
423:         impl Arbitrary for AsciiAlphanumeric {
424:             fn arbitrary(g: &mut quickcheck::Gen) -> Self {
425:                 let mut out = String::new();
426: 
427:                 let size = u8_between(1, 20, g) as usize;
428: 
429:                 while out.len() < size {
430:                     let c = char::arbitrary(g);
431:                     if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
432:                         out.push(c);
433:                     }
434:                 }
435:                 Self(out)
436:             }
437:         }

440:         assert!(!out.is_empty());

part.text:
Done. The fix removes trailing-slash redirect support from the router, matching the issue's request that unmatched paths (including trailing-slash mismatches) go to the fallback instead of redirecting.

Changes in `axum/src/routing/mod.rs`:
- `Router::call` (axum/src/routing/mod.rs:487): any `matchit` match error — including `MissingTrailingSlash` and `ExtraTrailingSlash` — now calls the fallback, so `/foo/` for a `/foo` route (and vice versa) returns 404 instead of a 308 redirect.
- Removed the now-unused `replace_path` helper, the `test_replace_trailing_slash` unit test, and the unused `Redirect`, `Uri`, and `IntoResponse` imports.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p axum`: all 201 lib tests pass, including `not_found_for_extra_trailing_slash`, `not_found_for_missing_trailing_slash`, and `with_and_without_trailing_slash`.
- Only 2 doc-test failures remain (`TypedHeader` examples), verified pre-existing on the untouched tree.
